title: Make allowed_paths bind real content: prose pathspecs silently collapse the frozen identity to the empty-set hash
objective: QUALIFYING EVIDENCE (session 14, 2026-08-11): M2-T016's allowed_paths are descriptive strings such as 'apps/web/src/** (survey review feature areas)' and 'services/api/app/documents/** (review-action endpoints + audit events only, disclosed)'. Those match nothing, so tools/directive_registry.py::frozen_git_identity returned e3b0c442...b855 - sha256 of the empty set - for a task shipping ~48 changed files. M0-T055 has the same shape (empty allowed_paths). SCOPE: (1) add a MECHANICAL guard that fails closed when a task's declared allowed_paths resolve to an empty tracked-file set while the task is not genuinely path-free - i.e. make the empty-set identity an explicit, surfaced condition rather than a silent pass; the guard must distinguish a legitimately path-free governance packet (which must then say so explicitly, e.g. an opt-in marker plus justification) from a code task whose pathspecs simply do not match; (2) wire it into the same fail-closed path submit/gate/accept already share, and into tools/validate_directive_compliance.py so CI catches it; (3) add regression tests covering: prose entry matches nothing -> REFUSE; valid pathspec -> identity is a real manifest hash; explicitly-declared path-free governance packet -> permitted with its justification recorded; (4) audit the EXISTING packets and report which ones currently stamp the empty-set hash, WITHOUT rewriting any accepted or in-flight packet - changing allowed_paths moves the material digest and would invalidate existing verification, so remediation of historical packets is a separate owner-visible decision, not part of this task. Correct nothing else.
business_reason: The directive-compliance acceptance gate is built on a frozen content identity computed from each task's allowed_paths. When those entries are prose rather than git pathspecs they match no files, frozen_git_identity returns the deterministic EMPTY-SET hash, and the identity binds NO code - so 'verified at this content identity' means nothing for that task, and the dirt guard also drops to an empty scope. This is a silent, undetected failure of the mechanism the whole D-001 regime depends on, discovered while accepting M2-T016 in session 14.

progress_log.message: AUDIT EVIDENCE captured at contracting (session 14, 2026-08-11, run against HEAD via directive_registry.frozen_git_identity with require_clean=False). NINETEEN packets currently stamp the deterministic EMPTY-SET identity e3b0c442...b855, meaning their frozen content identity binds NO tracked content. Two distinct causes. (A) NO allowed_paths at all (12): M0-T000 accepted, M0-T007 blocked, M0-T008 blocked, M0-T017 accepted, M0-T026 backlog, M0-T032 backlog, M0-T054 ACCEPTED, M0-T055 awaiting_gate, M0-T057 backlog (this packet - fixed below), M2-T019 backlog (fixed below), M4-T003 awaiting_gate, M2-T016 see (B). (B) PROSE / non-matching pathspecs (7): M1-T001 ACCEPTED, M2-T016 in_progress, M3-T002/T003/T004/T005 backlog, M4-T006 awaiting_gate, M6-T001 backlog. FOUR ARE ALREADY ACCEPTED - M0-T000, M0-T017, M0-T054, M1-T001 - so for those the recorded phrase 'independently verified at the reviewed content identity' is, mechanically, a statement about the empty set. That is the finding, stated plainly rather than softened. Most consequential: M0-T054 is the accepted turnover mechanism that M0-T056 (R595 production actuation) reuses and builds on. NOT REMEDIATED HERE, deliberately: accepted packets are immutable and editing allowed_paths on an in-flight packet moves its material digest and invalidates its existing verification, so retrofitting is an owner-visible decision, not a silent cleanup. This task's job is the MECHANICAL GUARD plus this audit; historical remediation is separate. NOTE the guard must not simply ban the empty set: a genuinely path-free governance packet is legitimate and must remain possible via an explicit opt-in marker with justification, which is exactly what distinguishes it from a code task whose pathspecs silently match nothing.
